question: Does strict patient-level temporal splitting reverse the ranking of transformer versus simple convolutional baselines on multi-centre 12-lead ECG arrhythmia detection?
brief:
## 1. Research Question
Does strict patient-level temporal splitting reverse the ranking of transformer versus simple convolutional baselines on multi-centre 12-lead ECG arrhythmia detection?

## 2. Why It Matters (and to Whom)
Clinical AI benchmarks routinely evaluate on random patient splits across pooled cohorts, inflating complex architecture gains that fail under calendar drift and cross-hospital transfer. Quantifying ranking reversals guides cardiology ML evaluation standards.

## 3. Closest Prior Work & What Is New
- Strodthoff et al. (2021, IEEE JBHI, 10.1109/JBHI.2020.3022989) benchmarked PTB-XL under random stratified folds.
- Reyna et al. (2021, PhysioNet Challenge, 10.1088/1361-6579/ac455a) tested multi-source generalization without calendar-year shift controls.
Delta: We pair strict temporal holdouts with cross-centre external validation across four open cohorts under matched preprocessing and calibration.

## 4. Data Sources & Access
- PTB-XL v1.0.3 (https://physionet.org/content/ptb-xl/1.0.3/, `direct`, free CC-BY 4.0; includes recording year and patient IDs).
- Chapman-Shaoxing 12-lead ECG (https://physionet.org/content/ecg-arrhythmia/1.0.0/, `direct`, free CC-BY 4.0).
All required rhythm labels and patient IDs are present in the direct releases.

## 5. First Decisive Test (Kill Test)
Download PTB-XL metadata and 2,000 stratified records (~1.5 GB, <= 2 CPU core-hours). Verify recording-year coverage and run a matched ResNet-1D vs lightweight transformer comparison on random vs temporal split.

## 6. What Result Would Kill This Topic
Freeze if recording dates are missing for >30% of patients (`data_access`) or if the random-vs-temporal AUROC ranking difference between architectures is <0.005 with overlapping 95% CIs (`negative_result`).
